Key Research Thinking Patterns: Unsupervised Contrastive Clustering for Patient Normalization: Leveraging self-supervised learning to group normal tissue patterns and separate lesion features, thereby reducing inter-patient variability without requiring paired healthy references (e.g., Achieving 76.47% high-risk lesion density in a single cluster compared to 38.89% with standard K-means).

Multitask Learning with Domain-Specific Fine-Tuning: Integrating diagnostic classification and segmentation tasks while addressing domain shift caused by tissue location bias through targeted fine-tuning (e.g., Improving overall model performance by 1.76% to 5.16% and reducing fairness gaps between oral locations by over 5%).

Label-Free Metabolic Imaging via Multi-Spectral FLIM: Utilizing dual-excitation frequency-domain fluorescence lifetime imaging to quantify biochemical changes such as redox ratios and NADH/FAD contributions for non-invasive tissue characterization (e.g., Detecting increased PpIX fluorescence and altered redox ratios in malignant oral lesions using a handheld endoscope).

Morphology-Enhanced Deep Transfer Learning: Incorporating explicit structural priors, such as mass contours, into pseudo-color representations to augment deep learning models for medical image classification (e.g., Achieving an AUC of 0.889 in breast mass classification by integrating manually segmented contours into VGG16-based models).
Summary Description: Javier Jo is a biomedical engineer specializing in the development of label-free optical imaging systems and AI-driven diagnostic tools for oral oncology and breast cancer screening. His research integrates multi-spectral autofluorescence lifetime imaging (maFLIM) with advanced machine learning techniques, including unsupervised contrastive learning and multitask neural networks, to address challenges in small datasets and inter-patient variability. Key contributions include the design of handheld endoscopic systems for real-time metabolic imaging and the creation of fairness-aware algorithms that mitigate tissue-location bias in clinical AI. By combining precise optical hardware with robust deep learning frameworks, his work aims to enable non-invasive early cancer detection, accurate tumor margin delineation, and equitable clinical decision support, significantly reducing the need for unnecessary biopsies and improving diagnostic accuracy in oral and breast pathologies.
